questions.question: Which of the following does NOT belong to the category of Porifera?
questions.solution:
Hydra does not belong to the category of Porifera; it belongs to the phylum Cnidaria (Coelenterata).
  • Porifera consists of sponges like Sycon, Euplectella (Venus flower basket), and Spongilla (freshwater sponge), which have a cellular level of organization and a canal system.
  • Hydra possesses a tissue level of organization and specialized stinging cells called cnidoblasts.

questions.question: Identify a spiral-shaped bacteria.
questions.solution:
Spirillum refers to spiral-shaped bacteria.
  • Bacteria are classified by shape: Coccus (spherical), Bacillus (rod-shaped), and Vibrio (comma-shaped).
  • These shapes are fundamental to their classification and how they move through their environment.

questions.question: What is the other name of tetanus caused by toxin producing bacteria called clostridium tetani?
questions.solution:
Tetanus is commonly known as Lockjaw.
  • It is caused by the bacterium Clostridium tetani, which produces a toxin affecting the nervous system.
  • The term 'Lockjaw' comes from the characteristic muscle spasms that cause the jaw to remain tightly closed.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of prokaryotic cells?
questions.solution:
Bacteria are the classic example of prokaryotic cells.
  • Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles.
  • Yeast is a fungus, and both Plasmodium and Leishmania are protozoans; all three are Eukaryotic.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best definition of ecological efficiency?
questions.option_1: The amount of energy stored at different trophic levels in a food chain
questions.option_2: The ratio between energy flows at different points in a food chain
questions.option_3: The ratio between the mass and the energy flow at different trophic levels in a food chain
questions.option_4: The amount of energy utilised at different trophic levels in a food chain
questions.solution:
Ecological efficiency is defined as the ratio between energy flows at different points in a food chain.
  • It typically describes the efficiency with which energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next.
  • On average, only about 10% of the energy is transferred to the next level (Lindeman's 10% law).

questions.question: Which is the most important protein component in milk, both quantitatively and nutritionally, that accounts for about 80% of the total protein in bovine milk?
questions.solution:
Casein is the most important protein in milk, accounting for about 80% of bovine milk protein.
  • It is nutritionally complete and provides the essential amino acids, calcium, and phosphorus needed for the growth of young mammals.
  • The remaining 20% of milk protein is generally comprised of Whey proteins like lactalbumin.

questions.question: Which of the following is related to Neem?
questions.solution:
Neem (Azadirachta indica) leaves are characterized as being Pinnately compound.
  • In pinnately compound leaves, a number of leaflets are present on a common axis called the rachis.
  • Note: In palmately compound leaves, leaflets are attached at a common point at the tip of the petiole (e.g., Silk Cotton).

questions.question: Which of the following is responsible for the red colour of beetroot?
questions.solution:
The red colour of beetroot is caused by a pigment called Betanin.
  • Betanin belongs to a group of pigments known as Betalains, which are different from the anthocyanins found in most other red plants.
  • Note: Lycopene is responsible for the red in tomatoes, and Beta carotene for the orange in carrots.

questions.question: By which of the following methods do red algae reproduce?
questions.solution:
Red algae primarily reproduce vegetatively through Fragmentation.
  • They can also reproduce asexually by non-motile spores and sexually by non-motile gametes (oogamous).
  • The lack of flagellated stages is a unique characteristic of red algae (Rhodophyceae).

questions.question: Identify an example of plasma as a state of matter.
questions.solution:
Neon sign bulbs are an example of the plasma state of matter.
  • Inside the bulb, gas gets ionized when electricity flows through it, creating a glowing plasma.
  • Note: Dry ice is solid CO2, and Freon is a gas/liquid refrigerant.

questions.question: Which of the following classes includes the family of turtles?
questions.solution:
Turtles are classified under the class Reptilia.
  • Reptiles are characterized by dry, cornified skin and epidermal scales or scutes.
  • Turtles are unique among reptiles for their bony or cartilaginous shell developed from their ribs.

questions.question: Which types of gametes are found in Spirogyra?
questions.solution:
Spirogrya produces gametes that are isogamous and non-flagellated.
  • Isogamous means the male and female gametes are similar in size and appearance.
  • In Spirogyra, these gametes lack flagella and move via a process called conjugation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Aves (birds) class?
questions.solution:
Pteropus (the Flying Fox/Fruit Bat) is not a bird; it is a mammal.
  • Neophron (Vulture), Struthio (Ostrich), and Psittacula (Parrot) are all members of the class Aves.
  • Bats are the only mammals capable of true sustained flight.

questions.question: What is the name of the inflammatory condition that causes cracks, crusting and scaling at the corners of the mouth due to vitamin B2 deficiency?
questions.solution:
Cheilosis is the inflammatory condition at the corners of the mouth caused by Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin) deficiency.
  • It is characterized by painful sores, cracks, and redness at the angles of the lips.
  • It is often accompanied by glossitis (inflammation of the tongue).

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of both mammals and birds?
questions.solution:
Being warm-blooded (homeothermic) is a characteristic shared by both mammals and birds.
  • Both groups maintain a constant internal body temperature regardless of the environment.
  • Differences: Mammals are generally viviparous (give birth to live young), while birds lay eggs. Birds have pneumatic (hollow) bones, which most mammals do not.

questions.question: In the context of cell division, which chromosomal behaviour takes place at the leptotene stage?
questions.solution:
During the leptotene stage of prophase I in meiosis, chromosomes begin to condense and become visible under the light microscope.
  • Leptotene is the first sub-stage of Prophase I.
  • Following this is zygotene, where homologous chromosomes begin to pair (synapsis).

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT regarding the grade of organisation and its example?
questions.solution:
The pair 'Tissue-organ grade organisation - Euplectella' is incorrect.
  • Euplectella (a sponge) has a Cellular grade of organization.
  • Tissue-organ grade is typically seen in Platyhelminthes (flatworms).

questions.question: Which condition, also known as icterus, causes a yellowing of your skin and the whites of your eyes?
questions.solution:
Jaundice (also known as icterus) causes the yellowing of the skin and eyes.
  • It occurs due to a buildup of bilirubin in the blood, often signaling issues with the liver, gallbladder, or pancreas.

questions.question: Hubbardia heptaneuron, which has become endangered, is a species of which of the following?
questions.solution:
Hubbardia heptaneuron is a rare and endangered species of Grass.
  • It was once thought to be extinct but was rediscovered in the Western Ghats of India.
  • It is endemic to specific spray zones of waterfalls.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?.
questions.solution:
The pair 'Starch: Egg yolk' is incorrectly matched.
  • Starch is a plant-based carbohydrate found in tubers (potatoes) and grains.
  • Egg yolk is primarily composed of lipids (fats) and proteins.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best defines the monoecious?
questions.option_1: A flower with both androecium and gynoecium
questions.solution:
A monoecious flower (or plant) is one that has both androecium and gynoecium (bisexual).
  • In a broader botanical sense, monoecious can also refer to a plant that has separate male and female flowers on the same individual.

questions.question: Which species is known as black lipped pearl oyster found in the Indo-Pacific, within tropical coral reefs?
questions.solution:
Pinctada margaritifera is the scientific name for the black-lipped pearl oyster.
  • It is highly valued for the production of 'black pearls' (Tahitian pearls) and is found throughout the Indo-Pacific.

questions.question: Which of the following categories does Gonyaulax belong to?
questions.solution:
Gonyaulax belongs to the category of Dinoflagellates.
  • Gonyaulax is famous for causing 'Red Tides' in the ocean, where rapid multiplication makes the water appear red.
  • These blooms can release toxins that are harmful to marine life and humans.

questions.question: Which marine carotenoid is abundant in brown seaweed, macroalgae and diatoms?
questions.solution:
Fucoxanthin is the marine carotenoid pigment abundant in brown seaweed (Phaeophyceae) and diatoms.
  • It gives brown algae their characteristic olive-green to brown color by masking the green of chlorophyll.

questions.question: Filtration of waste products in humans happens in the kidneys. There is a large number of filtration units present inside the kidneys to help them in doing this job. These filtration units are called:
questions.solution:
The functional filtration units of the kidney are called nephrons.
  • Each human kidney contains approximately one million nephrons.
  • The process involves filtration in the Bowman's capsule followed by selective reabsorption and secretion in the renal tubules.
